solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Farm implement thus redirected animal

parts.note: sic is the Latin word for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed

indicators.note: redirected means the animal's name is sent the other way, read backwards

parts.note: an elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: A farm tool somehow sends an animal off in a new direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redirected' sends the animal backwards; the surface pictures a herd being steered, but it only reverses the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved blade on a short handle used for cutting crops is a classic farm tool.

clue.text: Wise to guard boat, given unusually malicious damage

indicators.note: to guard something is to surround it, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a sage is a wise person, and sage also means wise

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of the following word arranged in an odd way

explanation.surface: A wise person protects a boat, which is unusually given some deliberate damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link word; 'unusually' shuffles the boat and 'to guard' wraps the wise piece around those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately wrecking equipment or plans is the standard meaning of the word for wilful damage.

clue.text: Primate from Central America climbed up part of one's body

parts.note: CA is a common abbreviation for Central America

indicators.note: in a down entry, a word that has climbed reads from bottom to top, so it is reversed

parts.note: taken as written
the chin is a part of the face

explanation.surface: A monkey from Central America has climbed up somebody's body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbed' turns UP into PU in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a South American monkey named for its hood-like crown, so it is a kind of primate.

clue.text: Forgetting paint has lid removed

indicators.note: a lid is the top, so in this down entry the first letter comes off

parts.note: gloss is a type of shiny paint

explanation.surface: Someone forgets that the paint pot has had its lid taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lid removed' takes the G off GLOSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is forgetting; the noun loss stands for the act of forgetting here, as in 'memory loss'.

clue.text: Time of year you and I head for Rome

parts.note: August is a month, a time of year
you and I together are us

explanation.surface: A season arrives and the two of us set off for Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head for Rome' looks like travel; it means a head of Rome, its first emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Roman emperor was the head of state of Rome, so he is a head for Rome.

clue.text: Disagreeing, Mourinho scuffled with an American

indicators.note: to scuffle is to tussle, so the letters of the following words are jumbled

parts.note: US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: A football manager, José Mourinho, gets into a scuffle with an American and they fall out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scuffled' rearranges MOURINHO plus AN into UNHARMONIO, and US ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of harmony with someone is a way of saying you disagree or clash.

clue.text: Top dog, on our ground, runs away, being mischievous

indicators.note: ground, as in ground down, signals the letters being broken up and remixed
away signals that the runs are taken out of the word our

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: The top dog runs off across our field, behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs away' removes R from OUR, leaving OU; 'ground' then remixes TOPDOG, ON and OU.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means engaged in some scheme or prank, which is behaving mischievously.

clue.text: Rat in an instant avoids Mortlake rowing

indicators.note: avoids means the letters of an instant are left out of the mix
rowing, as in a quarrel, suggests the letters of Mortlake thrown into disorder

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant

explanation.surface: A rat swiftly dodges the rowing at Mortlake, home of the Boat Race finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Take MO from the letters of MORTLAKE and 'rowing' rearranges the rest. Mortlake is the London district where the Oxford-Cambridge Boat Race ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat in slang is an informer, someone who talks to the police.

clue.text: Broadcast end of race to place in Africa

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it by scattering

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word race

explanation.surface: Broadcasting the end of a race to a place in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: This township near Johannesburg in South Africa is a well-known African place.

clue.text: Times article in footnote readers ultimately ignore

parts.note: times as in multiplication: six times two is six by two

indicators.note: in places the article within the footnote

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added at the end
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of readers

explanation.surface: A newspaper article sits in a footnote that readers end up overlooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A inside PS.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass round something rather than deal with it is to ignore or avoid it.

clue.text: Old politician starts to wage inquiry into distribution of wealth

indicators.note: the first letters go into the share-out of the letters of wealth, mixing them
starts to picks the first letters of wage and inquiry

explanation.surface: Someone launches an inquiry into how wealth is shared out.
explanation.walkthrough: W and I join WEALTH and 'distribution of' rearranges all eight letters. Willie Whitelaw was a senior British Conservative minister, deputy to Margaret Thatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: William Whitelaw was a British Conservative statesman of the 1970s and 1980s, so an old politician.

clue.text: Huge black heron flaps on river — it's a retreat for Victoria

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for very large
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

indicators.note: flaps suggests the letters of heron flapping about into a new order

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A huge black heron flaps its wings along a river where a queen might rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flaps' rearranges HERON into ORNEH. OSBORNE HOUSE on the Isle of Wight was Queen Victoria's holiday home.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria and Prince Albert built this seaside residence as a private refuge from court life.

clue.text: Food course

definitions.meaning: slang for food, as in hardtack, ship's biscuit
a course or line of action, from a sailing ship's zigzag heading

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: coarse fare is called tack, and a change of tack means a change of course.

clue.text: Trains drunken man to produce description of wine?

indicators.note: drunken signals letters staggering into a new order

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A drunk man on the train comes up with a wine review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' rearranges TRAINS into ASTRIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasters call a sharp, mouth-puckering wine this, so it serves as a tasting term, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Pretended to be Neil's estranged banking son

indicators.note: banking as in holding in a bank: the jumble keeps the son inside it
estranged means set apart, so the letters are separated and rearranged

parts.note: the name and its 's give the letters N E I L S
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone pretended to be Neil's estranged son, the one in banking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'estranged' rearranges TO BE and NEILS into OTENSIBLE, and S goes inside after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means professed or apparent rather than real, which matches a pretended reason or motive.

clue.text: Artist profits "nil", manager finally revealed in branch

parts.note: gains are profits

indicators.note: revealed in means shown inside, so these letters sit within the branch

parts.note: a bough is a tree branch
nil is zero, written as the letter O

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of manager

explanation.surface: A painter makes no profit at all, the manager eventually reveals at a branch office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealed in' puts O and R inside BOUGH. Thomas Gainsborough was an 18th-century English portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gainsborough was a celebrated English painter of portraits and landscapes.

clue.text: Lord entertaining caught last of the lake fish

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so caught goes inside

parts.note: the Lord as creator is the Maker
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the

parts.note: L is a map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A nobleman hosting guests has caught the last fish of the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts C inside MAKER.
explanation.definitionFit: This striped oily sea fish is a common food fish.

clue.text: Cheese worker admits lapse when cutting

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the jumbled letters go inside the worker

parts.note: a bee, especially a worker bee, is a crossword worker

indicators.note: cutting, as in cutting a deck of cards, signals the letters of lapse being shuffled

explanation.surface: A cheese factory worker admits a lapse while slicing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' is read as shuffling, as when a deck of cards is cut; 'when' is a link. Bel Paese is an Italian cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: This mild, soft Italian cheese has a name meaning beautiful country.

clue.text: Again strengthen control gate Ivor loosened

parts.note: to rein in is to control, and a rein is a means of control

indicators.note: loosened suggests the letters coming free and resettling in a new order

explanation.surface: Ivor loosened the gate, so control must be tightened again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosened' rearranges GATE and IVOR into VIGORATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To give fresh vigour is to strengthen once more, matching the re- prefix.

clue.text: Surrounded by a fog engulfing bottom of road

indicators.note: engulfing means swallowing up, so the letter goes inside the fog

parts.note: mist is a thin fog

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of road is its last letter

explanation.surface: Lost in a fog that swallows up the end of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engulfing' puts D inside MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means in the middle of, which is being surrounded by something.

clue.text: Feel guilty about exercise books

parts.note: re means about or concerning
PE is physical education, school exercise
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: Someone feels bad about their unfinished exercise books.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sorry for a wrongdoing and regret it is to feel guilty about it.

clue.text: Use hammer to repair outside cold pipe

indicators.note: outside means the jumbled letters go around cold
to repair is to fix up, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: Use a hammer to mend the outside of a cold pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures plumbing, but the pipe is a carved tobacco pipe; 'outside' wraps the remixed letters around the cold tap letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tobacco pipe carved from a soft white clay mineral of the same name.

clue.text: Avoid captain

definitions.meaning: to avoid or miss it out
the captain of a team, especially in curling or bowls

explanation.definitionFit: Skipping a lesson is avoiding it, and skip is short for skipper, the captain.

clue.text: Bird I see up in court

indicators.note: in places the turned exclamation inside the court abbreviation
in a down clue, up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: ah is an exclamation of understanding, like I see

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted flying up inside a court building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' only works because this is a down entry; the court is its two-letter abbreviation, not a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: The stonechat and whinchat are small songbirds, known collectively by this name.

clue.text: Computer lead, left alongside flower, fused regularly

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: here the Dee
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter, the second and fourth of fused

explanation.surface: A computer's lead and left-hand plug have fused together with a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river, something that flows; the Dee is a British river. 'alongside' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: IBM's chess-playing machine that beat Garry Kasparov in 1997 was a famous computer.

clue.text: Accuse cleaner, say, when returning

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a cleaner

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the abbreviation for say is read in reverse

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means in 'fruit, say'

explanation.surface: A cleaner is accused of something when she comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when returning' turns EG into GE. A char is British slang for a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with a crime is to accuse them formally of it.

clue.text: Glossy magazine editor, with latitude replaced by time in rags

indicators.note: replaced by means one letter is swapped out for the other

parts.note: Tatler is a British glossy society magazine
T is the physics abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A glossy magazine editor ends up in rags after a change of scope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced by' swaps the latitude letter for the time letter inside the magazine name; Tatler is a British society magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes torn into shreds are tattered, so to be in rags is to be in a ragged state.

clue.text: PM heading out of hostile conflict (eastern)?

indicators.note: heading out means the first letter, the head, leaves

parts.note: a battle is a hostile conflict

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister heads away from a hostile war in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading out of' drops the B from BATTLE. Clement Attlee was the British Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee led Britain's postwar Labour government as Prime Minister.
